bom_outlook.source: Bureau of Meteorology long-range forecast (ACCESS-S), written summary
bom_outlook.headline: Rainfall and temperature long-range forecasts
bom_outlook.rainfall_verdict: Above average rainfall likely for large parts of Australia, below average in parts of the far north and south-east
rainfall_for_state: November to January rainfall is likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) to be above average across most of southern and central Western Australia extending into southern parts of the Northern Territory, most of South Australia, southern Queensland and north-eastern New South Wales.
The wet signal is more pronounced in the west earlier in the season but strengthens in the east during December.
There is some variation in the likelihood of above average rainfall across the east between models.
bom_outlook.temperature_verdict: Above average temperatures likely across Australia
temperature_for_state: There is an increased likelihood (over 50% chance) of unusually high maximum temperatures 2 across much of Australia, with the highest chances (over 70%) across eastern parts of New South Wales and Victoria, eastern Tasmania, south-west Western Australia and Queensland's far north.
bom_outlook.point_how_to: Open https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/outlooks/#/rainfall/median, click the property on the map, and type the four 'chance of above median' percentages and the issue date into 'point' above (a number like 65 means 65%). They stay until the Bureau's next issue.
